sections.label: Consistency in competition regulation
sections.summary: The Bill brings greater consistency and clarity to competition regulation in the media and telecommunications sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: First, this Bill brings greater consistency and clarity to the regulation of competition in both the media and telecommunications sectors.

sections.label: Oversight over changes in control
sections.summary: The Bill strengthens oversight over changes in control, which the passage states is necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Second, this Bill strengthens oversight over changes in control, and that is necessary.

sections.label: Reducing unnecessary burdens
sections.summary: The passage supports reducing unnecessary burdens even while regulation is strengthened.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Third, I also support reducing unnecessary burdens even as we strengthen regulation.

sections.label: Minister's separation order power
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Minister issue separation orders in specific circumstances involving significant media resources, where IMDA action is insufficient and it is in the public interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Fifth, this Bill also introduces the power for the Minister to issue separation orders in specific circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, where a regulated person owns or controls certain significant media resources that are difficult to replicate, that may create barriers to market entry or that other competitors require in order to compete, and where actions taken or likely to be taken by the Infocomm Media and Development Authority (IMDA) are insufficient to address the problem, the Minister may issue a separation order where it is in the public interest to do so.

sections.label: Questions on divestiture and attractiveness
sections.summary: The passage asks the Government to elaborate on invoking divestiture powers as a last resort and on maintaining Singapore's attractiveness as a hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Fourth, for stronger powers, such as the divestiture order, will the Government elaborate further on the circumstances under which it would consider invoking such powers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: It would also be helpful to explain how the Government will ensure that this remains a measure of last resort, applied in a manner proportionate to the situation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Fifth, even as we promote fair competition, how do we continue to maintain Singapore's attractiveness as a hub for digital media, technology platforms and regional content?

sections.label: Trusted hub and algorithms
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore should remain a trusted and attractive hub for investment and innovation, and that influence is also about algorithms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But at the same time, remain a trusted and attractive hub for investment and innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: We should recognise that influence today is not just about ownership, but also about algorithms.

sections.label: Protecting smaller players
sections.summary: Strengthening regulation must ensure smaller players like startups, independent creators and community platforms are not crowded out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: As we strengthen regulation, we must ensure that smaller players, like startups, independent creators and community platforms, are not crowded out.

sections.label: Critical thinking and consultations
sections.summary: This Bill builds on public consultations concluded in January 2026 and follows the 2022 converged Code of Practice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Hong Chuang (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: When people are able to question, evaluate and think critically about what they see, they become an active part of a trusted digital ecosystem.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: This Bill builds on substantial public consultations that concluded in January 2026 and follows from the introduction of the converged Code of Practice for Competition in the Provision of Telecommunication and Media Services in 2022.

sections.label: Voiding anti-competitive provisions
sections.summary: Under the amendments, only provisions found anti-competitive will be void, with the rest of the agreement remaining valid.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Previously, where an agreement was found to be anti-competitive under section 62 of the IMDA Act, the entire agreement could be rendered void.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Under the proposed amendments, only the provisions found to be anti-competitive will be void, with the remainder of the agreement continuing to be valid and enforceable.

sections.label: Media-like entities and social media
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the competition framework may extend to media-like entities and about regulating social media use by adolescents and youths.

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: Given the increasing role of local digital media companies and content businesses in disseminating news and shaping public discourse, could the Minister share whether the Ministry is considering whether aspects of this competition framework may in time need to extend to entities that perform media-like functions even if they do not fall within traditional licensing categories?

sentences.speaker: Ms Cassandra Lee (West Coast-Jurong West)
sentences.text: In this context, as IMDA and the Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) continue to review and update the regulatory framework, I would like to ask if the Ministry would share any updates on whether it is considering any further developments in relation to the regulation of social media use by adolescents and youths.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: To recap what I said yesterday, the amendments are technical in nature but they are nonetheless important.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: They strengthen our regulatory toolkit to ensure fair competition and market conduct in the media sector and protect consumer interests.

sections.label: Trust in mainstream media
sections.summary: A 2025 Reuters Institute survey found Singapore's mainstream media outlets remained the most trusted news brands.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: A 2025 survey by the Reuters Institute found that our mainstream media outlets remained the most trusted news brands in Singapore.

sections.label: Consistent competition principles
sections.summary: Despite sector-specific nuances, the underlying principles are to constrain abuse of market dominance, facilitate fair competition and protect consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: While there will always be sector-specific nuances, the underlying principles and objectives are consistent, namely, to constrain the abuse of market dominance, facilitate fair competition and protect consumers.

sections.label: IMDA designation publicity methods
sections.summary: IMDA may communicate an essential resource designation by adequate publicity or notice, not only by Gazette notification.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The amendment provides that IMDA may communicate the designation of an essential resource in a manner to secure adequate publicity or notice rather than solely by notification in the Gazette.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: I say that because I think there was some confusion to think we are no longer publishing in the Gazette.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: We are, but in addition to that, we are publishing on IMDA's website and sending the notification directly to the affected party.

sections.label: Definition targets key media entities
sections.summary: The definition remains targeted at key media entities and covers only entities specified by the Minister in the Gazette.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The definition continues to be targeted at key media entities and only covers entities specified by the Minister in the Gazette.

sections.label: Limits on direction powers
sections.summary: The power to issue directions is limited to maintaining fair market conduct, effective competition and safeguarding consumer interests.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: To be clear, the power to issue directions must be read in the context of the full provisions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Thus, the power is limited to maintaining fair market conduct and effective competition and safeguarding consumer interests.

sections.label: Structural separation as last resort
sections.summary: Structural separations are intended only as a last resort in exceptional cases, and three requirements must be met before a separation order.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: While the provisions mirror existing powers in the Telecommunications Act, those powers have not been exercised to date.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: It is our intent that structural separations are only imposed as a last resort and in exceptional cases.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: All three of the following requirements must be met before a separation order can be issued.

sections.label: Separation order legal requirements
sections.summary: All legal requirements must be satisfied, reflecting intent that a separation order is a last resort after all regulatory tools fail.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: All of these legal requirements must be satisfied and no single requirement alone is sufficient.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: This reflects a clear legislative intent: a separation order is a last resort.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The Bill therefore ensures such powers may be exercised in defined circumstances, for defined purposes, and only after all regulatory tools have failed and only with directions that are proportionate to the competitive harm being addressed.

sections.label: IMDA assessment of major acquisitions
sections.summary: IMDA will consider whether an acquisition would likely substantially lessen competition or is against the public interest.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: To address Dr Choo, Mr Fadli and Mr Yip's questions on the new section 65, including how IMDA will assess major acquisitions, IMDA will consider whether the acquisition would likely result in a substantial lessening of competition or is against the public interest.

sections.label: Telecom sector mechanisms established
sections.summary: Both mechanisms are well established in the telecommunication sector since full market liberalisation in April 2000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Both mechanisms are already well established in the telecommunication sector, since the market was fully liberalised in April 2000.

sections.label: Public consultation on Bill
sections.summary: MDDI and IMDA conducted a public consultation for the Bill and received one submission from a law firm directly relevant to it.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: On this particular point, as mentioned by Mr Low, MDDI and IMDA conducted a public consultation for the Bill.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: By the close of the consultation, MDDI and IMDA received one submission from a law firm directly relevant to the Bill.

sections.label: IMDA powers not new
sections.summary: The powers are not new to IMDA, which has exercised equivalent powers judiciously in the telecommunications sector for years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Importantly, as I have explained, such powers are not new to IMDA – it has been exercising equivalent powers judiciously in the telecommunications sector for years.

sections.label: Online safety laws and codes
sections.summary: In 2022 the Broadcasting Act was amended, IMDA introduced Online Safety Codes of Practice in 2023 and 2025, and the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act established the Commissioner of Online Safety.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: For example, in 2022, we amended the Broadcasting Act, which allowed IMDA to issue directions to social media services to prevent Singapore users' access to egregious content on their platforms.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: IMDA also introduced Codes of Practice for Online Safety in 2023 and 2025 for designated social media services and app stores respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Last year, this House passed the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act, establishing the Commissioner of Online Safety to provide victims of online harms with timely relief and redress.

sections.label: Regulated persons under IMDA Act
sections.summary: Regulated persons under the IMDA Act are intended to be specific entities including SPH Media Trust, Mediacorp and Pay TV operators.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The regulated persons under the IMDA Act are intended to be specific entities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: These include major players, including SPH Media Trust, Mediacorp and our Pay TV operators.

sections.label: Amendments prevent unfair competition
sections.summary: The amendments act to prevent unfair competition and potential abuse of market dominance by large players that may frustrate other players' entry and growth in the media sector.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: Seen in this light, these amendments act to prevent unfair competition and potential abuse of market dominance by large players that may frustrate the entry and growth of other players in the media sector.

sections.label: Media co-production and business trips
sections.summary: IMDA's International Co-Production Fund supports local media companies, and the speaker joined business development trips to China and Korea.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: For example, IMDA's International Co-Production Fund supports local production houses and is awarded to local media companies to co-produce high quality drama series that are infused with a Singapore flavour and made for a global audience.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: In fact, I recently joined a trip with NTUC and brought a group of almost 30 content creators, freelancers, small media businesses, on a business development trip to Hangzhou and Hengdian, China, and brought another group of more than 10 larger local media companies to Seoul, Korea to look at collaboration opportunities.

sections.label: Bill procedures and regulatory transparency
sections.summary: The Bill sets procedures for measured use of powers, promoting fair markets and business certainty, and the speaker thanks Members.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: The Bill has established clear procedures to ensure that these powers are exercised only when necessary and in a measured manner, promoting a fair market environment while also providing businesses with certainty and confidence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: I also agree with Dr Choo Pei Ling that we must remain transparent in our approach to regulation, so as to ensure that industry players and the public continue to have confidence in our regulatory framework. : Sir, in conclusion, I thank Members for their thoughtful contributions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Digital Development and Information (Mr Tan Kiat How)
sentences.text: This Bill is necessary to promote fair competition and to continue safeguarding consumers' interests.

sections.label: Small player definition and regulated scope
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the small player definition and asks whether social media and foreign players with local presence are covered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We appreciate the definition of what the Ministry is considering a "small player" and where exactly where the threshold lies, because I think this speaks to our concerns about the chilling effect of the legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I also specifically had asked if this IMDA Bill, together with the Broadcasting Act that also is being amended, read together, does the scope of the regulated persons potentially include social media companies, foreign players, but that have a local presence?

sections.label: Podcasts and public interest concern
sections.summary: The speaker says podcasts may fall under regulated entities and raises concern about the public interest line in section 61A.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, it is well within conception that podcasts might well fall under a type of company or entity that may need to be regulated under these provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I also had a specific concern about the "in the public interest" line, in section 61A, para 1C.

sections.label: Separation order and licence reapplication
sections.summary: The speaker seeks clarification on whether separated independent media companies must reapply for licences or be transferred to a Government-linked company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, I would appreciate if Senior Minister of State Tan can clarify that that is not the intent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I had asked specifically if the Government will commit to not directing independent media companies that have been subject to a separation order, to then have that business transferred to a Government-linked media company.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If you read section 69A (3)b(ii) of the Bill, it seems to imply that companies that have been subject to a separation order will be obligated to reapply for their newspaper licence or broadcasting licence as the case may be.

sections.label: Broadcasting Act untouched
sections.summary: The amendment Bill does not affect the Broadcasting Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Nothing in this amendment Bill touches the Broadcasting Act.

sections.label: Fair competition and consumer interest
sections.summary: The regulatory intent is fair market competition and protecting consumer interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The regulatory intent is for fair market competition and protecting consumer interest.

sections.label: Challenging Minister's order decision
sections.summary: In exceptional circumstances where all measures failed, after the Minister decides and issues the order, the decision can be challenged and the Minister must defend it publicly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: Only in exceptional circumstances where all existing measures have failed – and I listed the three legal requirements for that before the Minister decides – and after the Minister decides and issues the order, the decision can be challenged; and the Minister needs to defend it publicly.

sections.label: Policy intent of the Bill
sections.summary: The considerations must return to the Bill's policy intent, which asks whether it enhances competition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
sentences.text: The considerations must go back to the policy intent of the Bill, which is: "Does it enhance competition?
